findings.stemStart: Every winter a pair of one-year canes is
findings.problem: The explanation said double Guyot 'suits wider spacing, which is why the Medoc classically trains it' and that single Guyot carries its load 'on one wire'. The Medoc and the Cote d'Or are both planted at about 10,000 vines per hectare, so wider spacing does not explain the Medoc's choice. Both forms also tie down on a single fruiting wire, so 'on one wire' sets up a false contrast.
findings.fix: The second sentence now reads: the double form spreads the crop along the wire on both sides of the head and is the Medoc's classic habit, while the single form lays one cane to one side, carries a smaller load and is the Cote d'Or's.
findings.source: Standard training geometry: Guyot simple and double both use one fruiting wire; Medoc and Cote d'Or planting densities are comparable

findings.stemStart: Short and quick-selling is the only safe shape
findings.problem: The stem gave its own answer away. It described the page as 'quick-selling' and then asked what the page's length is matched to (the answer: how fast each wine sells). A student could reply 'how quickly they sell' just by echoing the stem.
findings.fix: The stem now states the open bottle's few days and asks for the other term: 'With no preservation behind it, a bottle opened for the glass list stays honest for only a few days, so the page is kept short. What is its length being matched to?' The first rewording used 'two or three' and tripped compound_answer_problems, so it was replaced. The explanation was rewritten so it no longer just repeats the stem. Answer and accept list are unchanged. The build passes, check-similarity shows nothing flagged, check-stem-echo is clean, and the id moves.
findings.source: Review standard: a stem must not be answerable from its own words

findings.stemStart: Nine grams of sugar sit in a still
findings.problem: The last clause had the logic backwards. It said high-acid Chenin 'carries less sweetness on its label than the palate reports'. But the acidity concession exists so that the label word can follow the palate. What the label understates is the analysed sugar, not what the palate perceives.
findings.fix: The clause now reads: 'which is why a high-acid Chenin so often wears a drier word on its label than its sugar figure alone would earn.'
findings.source: EU Reg 2019/33 Annex III part B: sec up to 9 g/L when total acidity is within 2 g/L of the sugar, and demi-sec up to 18 g/L when it is within 10 g/L

findings.stemStart: Recorked and refrigerated, a botrytis wine can pour
findings.problem: The explanation called sugar 'a preservative in the jam sense' that 'denies microbes the water they need'. At 100 to 200 g/L the water activity barely moves. Sweet table wines are less stable microbially than dry ones, which is why they are bottled with more sulphur or sterile-filtered. The explanation also said they hold 'days longer than anything dry', which a dry fortified wine such as Sercial or amontillado disproves.
findings.fix: Rewritten: sugar is the buffer which, together with high acidity and the generous sulphur sweet wines are bottled with, slows the open bottle's decline, and the sweetness masks the first flavour costs of oxidation. The comparison is now limited to 'the safest unfortified by-the-glass category ... days longer than any dry table wine'. The answer (its sugar) and the accept list are unchanged.
findings.source: Wine microbiology: residual-sugar wines need higher free SO2 or sterile filtration because sugar at table-wine levels feeds yeast and bacteria rather than starving them

verdicts.stemStart: Every winter a pair of one-year canes is
verdicts.why: The original's causal claim was wrong: Medoc and Cote d'Or plantings are both dense, close to 10,000 vines a hectare, so wider spacing cannot be why the Medoc trains double Guyot, and both forms tie down on one fruiting wire. The new sentence keeps the correct attributions (Guyot double in the Medoc, Guyot simple in the Cote d'Or) and drops the false reason. The module docstring's banned word before 'cooperage' was also changed, to 'cooperage habit', in the same diff without a log entry; that is the house rule applied to unshipped prose and is kept.

verdicts.stemStart: Short and quick-selling is the only safe shape
verdicts.why: The stem change was needed, since 'quick-selling' handed over the answer and no explanation edit could fix that. But the replacement said the bottle stays honest for a few days 'so the page is kept short' and then asked what the length is matched to, so by the stem's own logic 'the few days of open life' was a right answer the grader refuses. The stem now reads 'With no preservation behind it, a bottle opened for the glass list stays honest for only a few days. Set against that window, what is the length of the page being matched to?', which makes the window the fixed side and asks for the other one. I also added turnover, rate of turnover, how fast it turns over and how quickly it turns over, the trade's own word for rate of sale, which the list refused. The reviewer's new explanation is kept. Build, stem echo and similarity (max 0.323) are clean; the id moves once relative to HEAD, as it already did.

verdicts.stemStart: Nine grams of sugar sit in a still
verdicts.why: The original was backwards. The acidity tolerance exists because high acid makes a wine taste drier than its sugar, so the label agrees with the palate and understates the analysis. The new clause says exactly that, and the 12 to 18 g/L demi-sec band with acidity within 10 g/L matches Reg 2019/33 Annex III Part B.

verdicts.stemStart: Recorked and refrigerated, a botrytis wine can pour
verdicts.why: The reviewer was right to drop the jam claim, because table-wine sugar levels barely lower water activity, and right that dry fortified wines outlast sweet ones. The rewrite brought in two new problems. It credited sugar itself with slowing the decline, when its real part is masking (sweetness and weight cover the first flavour costs of oxidation) and the chemical slowing comes from sulphur and acidity. It also said 'the wine's high acidity', which overstates Sauternes, and 'days longer than any dry table wine', which vin jaune, unfortified and dry, disproves. The text now gives sugar the masking role, gives the slowing to acidity and the generous bottling sulphur, and ends 'one of the safest by-the-glass categories in the building, outlasting the dry whites and reds poured beside it by days.' The answer and accept list are unchanged.
